QUARTERLY REPORT
22 MAY 2026
· CARDIGAN BAY
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

The seven hectares enclosed in spring 2023 are accreting at 11.4 mm of vertical gain per tidal cycle — well above the conservative forecast we drafted with University of Aberystwyth's coastal lab and reported in the 2024 prospectus.

What surprised the team was the early return of Salicornia europaea across the inner basin. Pages 4–11 of the field log set the data alongside drone transects and a frankly muddy account from the wardens.

Beaver dam analogues at Glen Lomas: first measurable channel widening.

Six analogues installed under permit last autumn are slowing winter spates and forming pool habitat. Catriona, our river ecologist, walks the bank with a tape measure and a useful dose of skepticism.

From the Caraghbeann fires: thirty hectares of old-growth burnt under permit conditions.

Controlled burns conducted with the Caraghbeann fire syndicate cleared 30 ha of mature stand on a long-deferred rotation. Charts compare biomass loadings before and after, plus the species census taken at four-week intervals.

Year-three actuarial audit, Loch Awe planting: 71.4% across 142,000 stems.

Survival of the 2023 native broadleaf planting is reported against the original prospectus thresholds. Year three is the moment growers find out which corners they cut cost them seedlings. The full audit is reproduced below, page by page.

· CUMBRIA

Donation reconciliation, August 2025: £.214 contribution matched, £1 pending review.

An accounting note: our August matching round, originally scheduled for Q4 2025, finally closes this month. We document where the lag came from, why it took eleven follow-ups, and what changes downstream of the audit.

02 APR 2026
· NORTH UIST
· 7 MIN READ
Peat re-wetting at Bordan Mire: water table holding within 4 cm of surface for 124 of the past 180 days.

The 2024 hag-rewetting on Bordan, machine-blocked last summer to plug 18 lateral runoff drains, has stabilised — the first sphagnum returnees were logged in mid-April. Page 11 reports the bench against last year's hydrograph.
